stories.title: US and Israeli strikes continue against IRGC-linked targets as Hormuz remains contested
stories.summary: Central Command reported additional strikes on Iranian Revolutionary Guard infrastructure. Oil futures reacted sharply; markets are pricing sustained risk of further disruption to the Strait of Hormuz, through which a large share of global crude still transits.

stories.title: Brent holds near $94–95 as energy security premium persists
stories.summary: Crude remains elevated relative to early-2026 levels after the spring Hormuz shock. Analysts note that even partial reopening of flows has not fully erased the risk premium while Iranian retaliation capacity and proxy activity remain active variables.

stories.title: Xi–Putin meeting at SCO reaffirms ‘solid’ partnership amid multipolar rhetoric
stories.summary: Chinese and Russian leaders used the Bishkek summit to emphasize closer coordination and criticism of ‘unilateralism.’ The optics reinforce the strategic alignment that has helped Moscow sustain its war effort and complicated Western isolation strategies.

stories.title: Ukraine expands deep-strike campaign against Russian energy infrastructure
stories.summary: Ukrainian long-range drones and missiles continue to hit refineries and logistics nodes inside Russia. The campaign aims to degrade revenue and logistics supporting the war; Moscow continues pressure on Ukrainian cities and energy systems in response.

stories.title: China maintains high tempo of PLA activity around Taiwan
stories.summary: Taipei reported elevated numbers of aircraft and vessels operating near the island, including median-line crossings. The pattern is consistent with sustained pressure short of kinetic action while Beijing tests response thresholds and domestic resolve in Taiwan and among partners.

stories.title: Equity markets soft as yields climb and oil firmness feeds inflation concerns
stories.summary: Major US indices closed lower. Higher energy costs and bond-market pressure are weighing on rate-cut expectations. Defense and energy sectors remain relative bright spots amid the broader risk-off tone.

stories.title: Sudan fighting intensifies around key North Kordofan positions
stories.summary: Army and Rapid Support Forces continue contesting strategic ground with high civilian cost. The conflict remains one of the world’s most severe humanitarian crises and a reminder that multiple high-intensity wars are running in parallel.

stories.title: Western capitals stress deterrence while managing escalation risks with Iran
stories.summary: Officials continue to balance the need to degrade Iranian proxy and nuclear-related capabilities against the risk of broader regional war. Energy markets remain the clearest real-time barometer of perceived escalation probability.

markers.title: Ukraine–Russia War
markers.detail: Full-scale conflict continues. Ukraine deep strikes on Russian energy/logistics; Russia pressures Ukrainian infrastructure and front lines. High strategic and humanitarian cost.

markers.title: Iran / Hormuz Theater
markers.detail: Direct and proxy exchanges with Israel and US forces. Strait of Hormuz risk remains the dominant global energy security flashpoint. IRGC-linked activity and residual nuclear concerns.

markers.title: Taiwan Strait Pressure
markers.detail: Sustained PLA air and naval activity around Taiwan, including median-line crossings. Critical semiconductor and Indo-Pacific deterrence node.

markers.title: Israel–Iran Axis Front
markers.detail: Multi-front posture against Iranian proxies and direct exchanges. High operational tempo since the 2023–26 cascade.

markers.title: Sudan Civil War
markers.detail: Army vs Rapid Support Forces. Intense fighting in North Kordofan and elsewhere. One of the world’s worst humanitarian crises.

markers.title: Yemen / Red Sea
markers.detail: Houthi activity and residual risk to Red Sea / Bab el-Mandeb shipping lanes. Intermittent cross-border strikes with Saudi Arabia.

markers.title: Myanmar Civil War
markers.detail: Ongoing multi-front fighting between junta and ethnic armed organizations / resistance. High civilian impact.

markers.title: Syria / Residual Conflict
markers.detail: Multiple overlapping actors; spillover risk from broader Iran–Israel and regional dynamics.

markers.title: Iraq – Militia Activity
markers.detail: Iran-aligned groups remain a pressure point; periodic strikes and political tension with Baghdad and US presence.

markers.title: Lake Chad / Sahel Insurgency
markers.detail: Boko Haram / ISWAP and other jihadist groups continue attacks across the Lake Chad basin and Sahel states.

markers.title: Eastern DRC
markers.detail: M23 and other armed groups; regional involvement (Rwanda/DRC tensions). Persistent displacement.

markers.title: Afghanistan–Pakistan Border
markers.detail: Cross-border friction and militant activity remain elevated after earlier ceasefire breakdowns.

markers.title: Central Asia Tensions
markers.detail: SCO region diplomacy concurrent with residual border and water-resource frictions among several states.

markers.title: Houthi Core Area
markers.detail: Command and logistics nodes tied to Red Sea interdiction capability.

markers.title: Strait of Hormuz
markers.detail: Critical chokepoint for global oil. Current risk premium is the main driver of elevated Brent (~$94–95). Any sustained closure would be systemically disruptive.

markers.title: Bab el-Mandeb / Red Sea
markers.detail: Secondary chokepoint. Residual Houthi threat continues to influence shipping insurance and rerouting costs.

markers.title: Persian Gulf Energy Complex
markers.detail: Major producers and export terminals. Saudi, UAE, Kuwait and others balancing security and market share.

markers.title: US Markets / NY
markers.detail: S&P ~7,631, VIX ~16.3. Defense and energy sectors relatively resilient amid broader risk-off.

markers.title: London / Europe Energy
markers.detail: European exposure to Middle East oil/gas disruption and elevated defense spending after Ukraine.

markers.title: Tokyo / Indo-Pacific Trade
markers.detail: Critical node for semiconductor and manufacturing supply chains; sensitive to Taiwan Strait risk.

markers.title: Hong Kong / South China Trade
markers.detail: Trade and finance hub under the shadow of Taiwan and South China Sea tensions.

markers.title: Singapore / Malacca
markers.detail: Major refining and shipping hub. Alternative route pressure when Hormuz or Red Sea risk rises.

markers.title: Dubai / UAE Energy Hub
markers.detail: Regional energy and logistics center; closely watches Hormuz and Iranian retaliation risk.

markers.title: Shanghai / China Export Hub
markers.detail: Manufacturing and export powerhouse. Sensitive to US–China trade and Taiwan contingency scenarios.
